notes.meaning: Solomon established his rule firmly over Israel, and the Lord was with him and made him very great. This fulfilled David's dying prayer that God would strengthen his son and bless his reign. True authority and lasting success come when the Lord supports and guides a leader.

Solomon called together all the leaders of Israel, including army commanders, judges, and family heads. He invited the whole nation's representatives to join him in a journey of worship. Good leaders use their influence to bring people together to honor God.

Solomon and the assembly traveled to Gibeon because God's sacred tent of meeting was there. Moses had built this tent in the wilderness as the special place where the Lord met with His people. Gibeon was honored above other places of worship because this historic sanctuary remained there.

David had earlier brought the ark of the covenant, the holy chest representing God's presence, to a tent in Jerusalem. This left the tabernacle tent at Gibeon while the ark rested in David's capital. Even though the two sacred items were separated, Solomon still sought the Lord at the ancient tent.

The bronze altar made long before by Bezalel was still sitting in front of the tabernacle at Gibeon. Solomon and the people gathered around it to pray and seek the Lord's favor. Coming to this altar showed that they approached God through animal sacrifices, just as the law of Moses instructed.

Solomon offered one thousand burnt offerings on the bronze altar through the priests. A burnt offering was a sacrifice completely consumed by fire to show wholehearted dedication to God. This massive offering demonstrated the king's deep devotion and the great importance of this national gathering.

During the night following the sacrifices, God appeared to Solomon in a dream and told him to ask for whatever he wanted. The Lord tested Solomon to reveal the true desires of his heart. God delights when His people bring their deepest needs to Him in prayer.

Solomon answered God by recalling the Lord's loyal love to his father David. He acknowledged that his position as king was not something he earned, but a gift from God. Remembering God's past faithfulness gives us confidence when we ask for His help today.

Solomon asked God to fulfill the covenant promise He had made to David. He felt humbled because he had to lead a nation as countless as the dust of the earth. Solomon recognized that he could only succeed if God remained faithful to His word.

Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge so he could lead the nation fairly. The phrase to go out and come in was a common way of describing a leader's daily duties in peace and war. Instead of seeking selfish advantage, he asked for the skill needed to serve God's people well.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Catholic Bible includes the Book of Wisdom, where chapter 9 gives an expanded version of Solomon's prayer and teaches that divine wisdom cannot be gained by human effort, but must be received through prayer.

notes.meaning: God praised Solomon because his heart did not desire selfish things like wealth, glory, long life, or revenge against enemies. Instead, Solomon cared most about understanding how to govern God's people properly. God notices and values the true motives behind our prayers.

God granted Solomon the wisdom he requested and also promised him unmatched wealth and honor. Because Solomon prioritized serving others, God freely added earthly blessings that no king before or after would equal. Putting God's will first opens the door to His unexpected generosity.

Solomon left the tent of meeting at Gibeon, returned to Jerusalem, and began actively ruling over Israel. He did not let his spiritual experience keep him from his practical duties. Worshiping God equips us to carry out our daily responsibilities with strength and purpose.

Solomon gathered 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses, placing them in chariot cities and keeping some with him in Jerusalem. This large army showed how God was fulfilling His promise of power and influence. Yet building such a large cavalry could also tempt a king to rely on military strength rather than the Lord.

Under Solomon's rule, silver and gold became as plentiful in Jerusalem as ordinary rocks, and prized cedar wood became as common as lowland sycamore trees. This striking picture illustrates the extraordinary wealth God gave to the kingdom. Material abundance is a gift from God, but it can also become a test of a nation's heart.

Solomon's royal merchants imported horses from Egypt and Kue, a region located in Cilicia. The king established official trade routes to buy these animals at regular prices. While this trade made the kingdom rich, God's law had warned Israel's kings against depending on horses from Egypt.

A chariot was imported from Egypt for six hundred silver coins and a horse for one hundred and fifty coins. Solomon's traders also resold these horses and chariots to neighboring Hittite and Aramean kings. Solomon used his position to create a profitable international business that supplied neighboring nations.
